summary: Intermittent truncation & 95p latency spikes after enabling aggressive kv_prefetch + mixed-quant profile on Dedicated pool
description: Customer ClearedSky enabled an aggressive optimizer profile (kv_prefetch=high, dynamic_batching=aggressive, quant_profile=mixed-int8-fp16) on their Dedicated capacity pool to reduce per-token cost. After rollout (traffic split 20%->60% over 6 hours) they report intermittent streaming truncations (response cuts before EOS) and a 95th-percentile token-generation latency spike from ~120ms to 420ms on long-sequence requests. Issue affects both chat and streaming generation endpoints. Customer is requesting prioritized assistance for a safe, stepwise rollback plan and an immediate mitigation to restore SLOs while preserving tenant state snapshots.
steps_to_reproduce: Deploy profile: kv_prefetch=high, dynamic_batching=aggressive, quant_profile=mixed-int8-fp16 to customer Dedicated pool
Route ~50% of steady-state traffic to the optimized profile (same tenant traffic patterns used by ClearedSky)
Send mixed-length prompts including long-history chat (seq len 1024-2048) and streaming response mode
Observe intermittent truncation (clients see "[STREAM END]" before full completion) and 95p latency spikes in provider metrics

investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: mixed-quant profile causing inconsistent kernel selection leading to thread contention and unhandled fallback that sometimes drops KV cache entries mid-request

KV prefetch 'high' increases cache churn for long-history requests; eviction interacts poorly with aggressive batching timeouts -> partial batches flush -> sequence reassembly issues in streaming layer
Observed runtime fallback traces where quant_runner falls back to a slower, non-vectorized kernel path for certain layer shapes when int8+fp16 mixes across partition boundaries
Simulated repro in staging with synthetic long-history requests reproduced 95p latency when quant fallback + high prefetch enabled together
No immediate GPU OOM or driver errors observed; CPU-side scheduler timeouts are prominent in the traces
temporary_workarounds: Reduce kv_prefetch from 'high' -> 'moderate' for affected tenant (recommended immediate action)
Temporarily disable mixed-quant profile (revert to fp16 only) for traffic above 30% on the Dedicated pool to avoid kernel fallback path
Lower dynamic_batching aggressiveness (increase target batch wait from 10ms -> 40ms) to reduce partial flush frequency
Enable per-tenant request sampling for end-to-end traces to capture full streaming lifecycle for impacted sessions
recommended_rollback_plan: Step 0 — Safe snapshot: capture current optimizer config snapshot (console -> tenant config -> export) and a serving runtime snapshot (config SHA + node assignments). Store in tenant artifacts before any change
Step 1 — Shadow revert: create a 'shadow' config that sets kv_prefetch=moderate, quant_profile=fp16, dynamic_batching=standard; keep it inactive
Step 2 — Canary swap: route 5% of traffic to shadow config for 15 minutes and monitor latency 95p, stream truncation rate, and cache miss rate
Step 3 — Gradual ramp: if canary is stable, incrementally increase to 30% over 30 minutes watching SLOs and error budget; keep rollback reversible at each step
Step 4 — Full flip if stable: after 2 hours at 30% with no regressions, promote shadow config to 100% and mark original snapshot as archived for audit
Step 5 — Post-change validation: run a short synthetic job covering long-history streaming and confirm EOS rates, latency percentiles, and no quant fallback traces

Rollback safety notes: apply per-node drain-control and avoid restarting model processes during config swap to preserve KV cache where possible; if restart unavoidable, coordinate with customer for short maintenance window
Operator commands: use 'rwi config export --tenant cleardsky --name pre-rollback-2026-03-12' and 'rwi traffic split --tenant cleardsky --set 5%:shadow-rollback' (see runbook links)
